errors.english: One cannot refute direct perception because one cannot refute an inference
errors.why: The Tibetan says that one who has not refuted perception cannot refute an inference from a mark established by it; the English inverts the dependency.

errors.english: with the object that is directly removed
errors.why: bsal ba here stands for vivid/manifest (the next side asks how something can be both vivid and conceptual), so the sense is 'a directly manifest object', not 'removed'; the same error recurs in 'remove the object of direct perception'.

errors.english: because they lack the causal power found in direct perception
errors.why: The comparison is with inference: other conceptions lack the capacity that inference has.

fix.find: because they lack the causal power found in direct perception
fix.replace: because they lack the capacity that inference has

errors.english: a person like Maitreya, merely by recognizing someone once
errors.why: byams pa is the stock example name Maitra, and he is the person occasionally recognized, not the one who recognizes.

note: The argument is broadly followed, but the bsal ba term and several logical relations between perception and inference are garbled.

errors.english: At the conclusion of the speech
errors.why: The line says that when the gods' cry of 'well done' to the king spread to the ends of the directions; the sense of it spreading to the ends of the directions is lost.

note: A sound rendering of the Tibetan verses, with the Sanskrit correctly kept in notes.

errors.why: In the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya the Sanskrit term saṅghāvaśeṣa is meant, not the Pali form.

errors.english: in order to show the reversal for those who wish to avoid blame
errors.why: The sūtra is cited to refute those who hold that the offence at that stage is a lower one (smad pa), not to address people who wish to avoid blame.

note: A generally faithful rendering of a technical Vinaya commentary, with a Pali term and one misread purpose clause.

errors.english: when it perceives an appearance in what is called the (essential mind) tattva-buddhi
errors.why: de kho na zhes bya ba quotes the root-text word 'that very' and refers to the cognition; it is not a technical 'tattva-buddhi'.

errors.english: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken.
errors.why: phyi rol pa rnams is a quoted root-text word meaning 'external things' (glossed as svalakṣaṇas), stated because others might not grasp the intent; these are not externalist opponents speaking.

fix.find: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken.
fix.replace: Since others might not understand the intention, he said "the external ones" and so forth.

errors.english: the commentators and others offer a reply
errors.why: The text answers with the root-text words 'the expounders' and so on; it is not commentators who reply.

note: The main svalakṣaṇa/sāmānya point comes through, but quoted root-text words are misread as technical terms or as speakers.

errors.english: The word "self" [note: original: "rang nyid"] is used in the sense of "also."
errors.why: It is the particle ni that has the sense of 'also'; rang nyid (svayam) is glossed separately as 'in itself'.

fix.find: The word "self" [note: original: "rang nyid"] is used in the sense of "also."
fix.replace: The particle "ni" is used in the sense of "also."

note: A faithful rendering of the commentary on svayam in the definition of the thesis, apart from one misassigned grammatical gloss.

errors.english: [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
errors.why: 'Indra's head' (śakramūrdhan) is the standard Pramāṇavārttika term for an anthill.

fix.find: [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]

errors.why: lci ba is cow dung (gomaya), the classic example of a dissimilar cause from which a lotus or similar plant arises.

errors.english: Fire is the nature of the cause of smoke, possessing the specific capacity for it.
errors.why: The two summary verses are run into prose.

note: The causal argument is followed, but the two classic examples (anthill, cow dung) are mistranslated.

errors.english: caused his body to be illuminated with supreme clarity
errors.why: 'Supremely radiant' (śuddhavaraprakāśaḥ) is an epithet of the Tathāgata, who out of devotion performed worship of his father's body; he did not illuminate the body.

fix.find: caused his body to be illuminated with supreme clarity. Out of devotion, he performed the funeral rites
fix.replace: supremely radiant, out of devotion performed worship of his body

errors.english: The one who serves the feet of the Great One is sustained in this world and the next
errors.why: The clause saying that it alone is worthy of praise among days is not rendered.

note: The narrative is right, but the Buddha's epithet is turned into an act of illuminating the body.

errors.english: not motivated by the view of the noble, supramundane, noble self
errors.why: 'Noble, supramundane' describes the right view itself; the views that do not motivate it are views of self, sentient being, and so on.

note: A sound rendering of the Akṣayamati quotation and the argument about latencies.
A faithful rendering of the general and specific characteristics of the four truths.

errors.english: lacking any limb [note: or part] that does not look upon her faults as virtues
errors.why: yan lag med pa is the 'Bodiless one' (Anaṅga, Kāma), who wastes their body day by day; it is not a lack of limbs.

errors.english: They would embrace a woman even if she were covered in sparks from a blazing fire born of iron.
errors.why: This is the hell torment of embracing blazing iron women covered in sparks, not a hypothetical about the lustful man's passion.

note: The sermon against desire is usable, but several of the verse images (Anaṅga, the hell punishment) are misread.
